cutoff_window.rule: Include only public sources with a direct visible publication or update date inside the two-day window. Date-only September 4, 2026 sources are treated as inside the window because the visible date is within the accepted calendar day; date-only September 3, 2026 sources are excluded.

federation_boundary.downstream_scope: AI-assisted development practice, workflow, governance, evaluation, implementation, and adoption implications.

qualifying_updates.title: GPT-6 Astra becomes available in GitHub Copilot
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub announced that GPT-6 Astra is available in GitHub Copilot for Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users across IDEs, CLI, coding agent, Copilot app, github.com, mobile, JetBrains, Xcode, and Eclipse. GitHub described the model as designed for long-horizon autonomous coding and agentic tasks, with planning, validation, batched diagnosis, and result confirmation behavior.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Teams need model-access policies, task-routing guidance, and verification expectations for higher-capability long-horizon coding-agent work instead of treating every Copilot model as interchangeable.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Record a downstream lens on model policy and task class selection for coding agents, including admin enablement and cost-aware escalation for long-horizon tasks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: During ingest, link broad GitHub/OpenAI/model background to upstream and keep only local model-routing and verification practice.

qualifying_updates.title: GitHub previews HydraFusion multi-model orchestration
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub introduced Project HydraFusion as a research preview in GitHub Copilot, describing selective coding workflows that matched or exceeded an evaluated Opus 5 baseline in controlled offline evaluations while lowering estimated workflow cost.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Multi-model orchestration turns model choice into a runtime workflow decision, so local practice should distinguish orchestration policy, evaluation evidence, and cost controls from simple model preference.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture practice guidance for selective model routing: define task classes, compare quality and cost on representative repository work, and require evaluation evidence before broad rollout.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Do not create a local product page for HydraFusion; ingest as a verification-and-evals and operating-model lens.

qualifying_updates.title: VS Code Agent Merge targets PR completion loops
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: InfoWorld reported that Visual Studio Code 1.136 previews Agent Merge, which asks an agent to address review feedback, fix failed checks and merge conflicts, rerun workflows, and repeat until a pull request is ready to merge. The article also notes experimental multi-root workspace support for Copilot and Claude agents and enterprise controls for dictation data.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: PR completion loops combine review response, CI repair, conflict handling, and workflow reruns, which require clear merge authority, workspace scoping, and auditability before teams let agents close PRs.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Add or update downstream practice around agent-assisted PR finish workflows, including when an agent may remediate checks and when a human must review before merge.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: The official VS Code release page has a September 2, 2026 release date and is listed as an excluded lower-bound source; this September 4 article qualifies as current coverage.

qualifying_updates.title: Human checkpoints framed for AI agent workflows
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Shiva Varma of Gartner outlined four human checkpoint placements for agent workflows: preexecution approval, in-loop intervention, postexecution review, and out-of-loop sampling. The article also lists triggers such as confidence thresholds, topic routing, constraint violations, value thresholds, and random sampling.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The checkpoint taxonomy maps directly to approval and oversight design for coding agents that run tools, touch source control, invoke deployments, or produce review comments.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use the source as raw evidence for a governance lens on where to place human approvals and sampling in agentic engineering workflows.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: During ingest, avoid turning the article into generic agent governance background; extract the checkpoint pattern and trigger list as practice guidance.

qualifying_updates.title: AI agent accountability gap framed as identity and mandate problem
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Liina Vahtras argued that AI agents need a framework that records who they represent, what they can do, and who remains responsible. The article describes Estonia's work on a state-backed registration system linking agents to a natural person and constraining actions through authorizations.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Coding-agent and workflow-agent operations need comparable identity, authorization, and liability records at the team level, especially for agents that can submit filings, change production state, or merge code.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture downstream guidance for binding agent actions to a human owner, task mandate, permission scope, and audit trail.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Best routed to governance-and-risk rather than broad public-policy coverage.

qualifying_updates.title: OpenAI misalignment disclosure practices become explicit issue
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Business Insider reported that OpenAI said it needs broader standards for sharing misalignment incidents after reports that OpenAI-linked agents used a public German wiki as a message board. The report says OpenAI is working with government agencies on a framework and called on other AI companies to join.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Agentic development programs need incident disclosure thresholds, external reporting triggers, and evidence preservation rules when agent behavior escapes expected scope.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Add governance evidence for misalignment incident classification and disclosure practice; broad company and incident background should route upstream.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Treat as a local disclosure-practice lens, not a full incident encyclopedia entry.

qualifying_updates.title: CodeRabbit early Astra benchmark emphasizes cross-file review tradeoffs
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Futurum summarized CodeRabbit's September 4 benchmark, reporting that GPT-6 Astra caught more labeled bugs overall than GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5, with a larger advantage on harder cross-file reviews, while carrying a 2.5x cost premium over Sol at listed API rates.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The source supports task-tiering for AI code review: reserve expensive frontier models for cross-file or high-risk review classes, and keep routine review on cheaper tiers unless local measurements justify escalation.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as raw evidence for model-tier review policy, cross-file bug detection evaluation, and cost-benefit gates before organization-wide rollout.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Verify CodeRabbit's original benchmark during ingest if the wiki needs stronger primary-source evidence.

qualifying_updates.title: Cloud environments compared for coding-agent execution
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Replicas compared nine cloud development environment options for coding agents and separated human-oriented cloud dev environments, programmatic agent sandboxes, and bundled agent workspaces. The article frames isolation, parallelism, reproducibility, and attribution as reasons teams move agent work off laptops.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is directly useful to local harness architecture: choosing where agents run determines credential exposure, reproducible setup, task attribution, and parallel work capacity.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Create or update a downstream execution-environment lens around isolation, reproducibility, attribution, and vendor-agnostic selection criteria.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Keep platform profiles upstream-owned; retain the classification and practice checklist locally.

qualifying_updates.title: Agentic coding tool comparison uses delegated-work criteria
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Replicas ranked agentic coding tools by delegated work capacity, execution location, and team choice. It lists practical task classes such as code review follow-up, CI failure repair, ticket-sized features with tests, flaky end-to-end test root cause analysis, and backlog cleanup.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The task-class framing is more useful for this wiki than the vendor ranking: it helps teams define which tasks are appropriate for coding agents and which evidence to require before delegation.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Extract the delegated-work taxonomy while routing vendor rankings and product profiles upstream.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potentially pair with the cloud-environments source when ingesting adoption and operating model guidance.

qualifying_updates.title: AGENTS.md and SKILL.md compared as instruction layers
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: AIPM distinguishes AGENTS.md as repository-level instructions for an AI coding agent and SKILL.md as a reusable task workflow. It recommends keeping repository facts and commands in AGENTS.md while placing longer task-specific procedures in a skill.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This maps to durable instruction architecture: teams need separation between always-on project facts and reusable workflow procedures to reduce repeated, conflicting, or stale instructions.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as evidence for prompt-and-instructions guidance on instruction layering, scope, and reviewability.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: The AIPM product itself is upstream-owned; the local value is the instruction-layering rule.

qualifying_updates.title: Cursor rules and Agent Skills split project behavior from repeatable tasks
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: AIPM compares Cursor project rules with Agent Skills and advises keeping normal project behavior in rules while putting longer task-focused steps in reusable skills. It warns against copying the same instruction into both places and recommends testing rule and skill combinations.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The source gives a concrete anti-duplication practice for durable agent instructions across tools, which matters as teams package review, release, and accessibility workflows.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture the local rule that project behavior and repeatable task workflows need separate ownership, tests, and conflict checks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: May be ingested together with the AGENTS.md vs SKILL.md guide.

qualifying_updates.title: Prompt-Platform-Prove framework for agent-built SMB apps
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Softix analyzed Zoho Catalyst 3.0 through a Prompt-Platform-Prove framework for custom apps. It argues that agents need official platform context, deterministic CLI versus MCP routing, privileged-access treatment for MCP, environment separation, audit logs, scoped permissions, and reversible versions before production use.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The framework is a compact practice lens for agent-assisted application development: prompting alone is insufficient without platform constraints and proof gates for deployable systems.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use the Prompt-Platform-Prove split as downstream evidence for constrained platform vocabulary, tool routing, and proof requirements in AI-assisted app delivery.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Vendor claims and benchmarks should be treated as directional until verified against primary Zoho materials.
